To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the integration of virtual environments with high-performance computing is possible and will benefit both fields.

virtual environments can be integrated with HPC by: (a) defining the requirements for the integration; (b) designing and implementing the infrastructure to meet these requirements; (c) designing and implementing a set of tools to use the infrastructure; and (d) using these tools to demonstrate the integration.

virtual environments and high performance computing can be naturally integrated by means of a multilashing objectoriented visual interactive environment, and that the resulting environment will be a powerful tool to solve grand challenge problems in science and engineering.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of interactive HPC systems, which we call virtual HPC systems.
the design of a new class of interactive environments that are capable of dynamically integrating virtual environments and high performance computing resources.
the development of an HPC infrastructure layer that will enable the seamless integration of HPC and virtual environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
virtual environments are not only the future of human-computer interaction but also a powerful tool for HPC, and vice versa.
the integration of virtual environments and HPC is not just a natural evolution but a requirement for the development of the next generation of virtual environments.
virtual environment technology is a key enabling technology for HPC, and vice versa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration between virtual environments and HPC is a natural one and that the MOVIE system is a suitable candidate to address the design issues.
MOVIE is a software infrastructure layer that enables the development of dynamic, distributed, and interactive HPC systems.
MOVIE is the first system to address the design issues that we have discussed in the previous sections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of the MOVIE system is based on an architecture that is well-suited to address the integration issues between HPC and virtual environments.
virtual environments can be effectively integrated with high performance parallel computing systems, provided that a suitable middleware is developed.
virtual environment front- ends and high performance computing resources are natural partners.
